Is Broadcom (AVGO) the Other AI Trade?
By IPO Edge Editorial Staff
Broadcom's (AVGO) AI business is growing faster than almost anyone expected.
Last quarter, AI semiconductor revenue hit $10.8 billion, up 143% year over year. Management expects that to reach $16.0 billion this quarter, a jump of more than 200%.
That is the kind of number that gets noticed.
Broadcom landed third among semiconductor searches by financial pros last month, behind only NVIDIA and Micron, according to our TrackStar data.
READ MORE
Highlights: Tech Edge at Pax8 Beyond 2026 in Salt Lake City
The stock isn't cheap. But the growth is real, the cash flow is enormous, and the AI story is just getting started.
Here's our take.
Broadcom's Business
Broadcom designs the custom chips and networking gear that move data inside the world's largest data centers.
What sets it apart is range. The company holds roughly 18,000 patents across 24 category-leading divisions, spanning silicon and software.
Its customers include hyperscale cloud providers, telecom carriers, and enterprise IT departments. Broadcom spent $11.0 billion on R&D in FY25 to keep that edge sharp.
Broadcom segments its business into the following areas:
-
Semiconductor Solutions (68% of total revenues) – Custom AI accelerators (XPUs), AI networking, broadband, server and storage chips, wireless, and industrial silicon
-
Infrastructure Software (32% of total revenues) – Cybersecurity, enterprise and mainframe software, Fibre Channel networking, and the VMware private cloud platform
Second quarter revenue rose 48% year over year to a record $22.2 billion. Semiconductor revenue jumped 79% as AI demand surged, while software grew a steadier 9%.

articles.headline: Micron Advances New York Chip Project
articles.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Micron Technology (MU, Financials) is pushing forward with its major chip project in Clay, New York, naming Bechtel as its construction partner.
The plant is expected to become the largest semiconductor manufacturing facility in the U.S. once completed. Micron broke ground on the site in January.
The facility will make advanced memory chips, which are used in data centers, phones, computers and AI systems. That makes the project important not just for Micron, but also for the broader U.S. chip supply chain.
For investors, this is a long-term story. The New York project will take time to build, but it shows Micron is preparing for future demand and a larger role in domestic semiconductor production.

articles.headline: Micron Moves Ahead With Massive New York Fab
articles.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) is moving ahead with its New York semiconductor project, naming Bechtel as the construction partner for the massive memory fab.
The facility is being built in Clay, New York, where Micron broke ground in January. Once completed, the project is expected to become the largest semiconductor manufacturing facility in the U.S., with a focus on leading edge memory production.
For Micron, the project is about more than adding capacity. It gives the company a bigger U.S. manufacturing footprint at a time when AI demand is increasing the need for advanced memory chips. Bechtel's role also gives the buildout a major construction partner as Micron works through one of its most important long term expansion plans.
For investors, the takeaway is straightforward: Micron is still building for a much larger memory cycle, even if the payoff will take time. The next thing to watch is how quickly the New York project moves from groundbreaking to major construction milestones.

This Semiconductor Stock Has More Than Tripled This Year – But Wolfe Research Sees Another 36% Upside
-
Wolfe raised its Micron forecasts to reflect an approximately 45% increase in memory pricing in the third quarter and stronger pricing trends through 2026.
-
The firm also raised its calendar 2027 projections for Micron, citing higher-than-expected pricing for high-bandwidth memory.
-
Wolfe now forecasts Micron will generate $226.5 billion in revenue and earn $135 per share in 2027.
Shares of Micron Technology Inc. (MU) are up nearly 217% year-to-date, but analysts at Wolfe Research expect the stock to rally further this year.
According to TheFly, Wolfe raised its price target for Micron to $1,250 from $550, implying an upside potential of about 36% from current levels. The firm maintained its 'Outperform' rating on the stock.
Micron shares were up more than 3% in Thursday's opening trade.
Why Is Wolfe Bullish On MU?
Wolfe raised its Micron forecast to reflect an approximately 45% increase in memory pricing during the fiscal third quarter (Q3), with stronger pricing trends expected to persist through calendar year 2026. The firm also raised its calendar 2027 projections for Micron, citing higher-than-expected pricing for high-bandwidth memory (HBM).
As a result, Wolfe now forecasts Micron will generate $226.5 billion in revenue and $135 in earnings per share (EPS) in 2027. While fiscal year 2026 is still ongoing, in the last completed fiscal year, 2025, Micron reported $37.4 billion in revenue and an EPS of $8.29.
Analysts at Daiwa raised their price target on Micron to $1,600 from $700 on Wednesday, while maintaining their 'Buy' rating on the stock.

articles.headline: Nasdaq, S&P Drop 1%, Dow Sinks 600 Points as Trump Iran Threat Sparks Market Panic
articles.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
U.S. equities fell Wednesday after geopolitical tensions rose following comments from President Donald Trump on Iran. Selling pressure intensified as major indexes moved sharply lower during the session.
U.S. equities saw broad declines, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropping 600 points, or 1.2%, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite fell 0.9% and 1.1%, respectively.
Markets weakened further after renewed rhetoric on Iran escalation from President Trump, which lifted risk concerns across trading desks. Crude prices rose as West Texas Intermediate futures climbed nearly 3% above $90 a barrel.
U.S. equities technology shares led declines, with semiconductor names extending recent losses. Micron Technology, Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom all traded lower for a fourth time in five sessions. Traders also cited portfolio rotation tied to upcoming SpaceX IPO expectations and recent profit-taking after strong year-to-date gains in the chip sector.
U.S. equities trimmed losses after softer-than-expected core inflation data, though annual inflation remained elevated above the Federal Reserve's target. Investors remained cautious amid heightened geopolitical uncertainty.

articles.headline: Seagate Stock's High-Density Gamble
articles.text:
The company is telling a story of explosive AI-driven growth, but its strategy for meeting it is what has Wall Street truly captivated.
When a company tells you the next quarter's earnings will jump 47% sequentially, you listen. When they say revenue will climb 19% in the same period, you pay attention. And when Seagate (STX)'s management did just that on Apr 28, 2026, the market did more than listen; it sent the stock soaring +46.1% since.
On the surface, this is a simple story of an AI-driven data boom. But look closer. The real question isn't if Seagate is growing, but how. The company is riding one of the hottest demand waves in tech, yet its core strategy is to meet it by making its hard drives denser, not by making more of them. Is this a masterstroke of profit leverage, or a dangerous cap on growth?
A New Era Of Growth
First, let's be clear about the scale of the story management is telling. They believe Seagate is now "entering a period of structural growth." Is this just talk? They backed it up by raising their annual revenue growth target from the mid-teens to "a minimum of 20% over the next few years." This is the kind of confident, long-term signal that gets investors to re-evaluate what a company is worth. The narrative is that the insatiable data appetite of AI isn't a temporary spike; it's the new normal.
More Data, Not More Disks
Here's where it gets interesting. In a gold rush, you expect miners to buy more shovels. But Seagate plans to build a better shovel. Management has been direct: "The total number of units is not really increasing." Instead of ramping up unit production, the entire focus is on areal density, cramming more and more terabytes onto each disk. This strategy has a profound effect on the financials. By selling more capacity without a proportional increase in materials or factory output, margins have exploded. The company's operating margin now sits at 29.5%, a world away from its 12.2% 3-year average.

articles.headline: Micron Jumps on Wolfe Target Raise
articles.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Micron Technology (MU, Financials) shares rose in premarket trading after Wolfe Research sharply raised its price target, citing stronger pricing across key memory markets.
Analyst Chris Caso lifted his target to $1,250 from $550 while keeping a Buy rating on the stock. The new target suggests about 40% upside from recent levels.
The upgrade is tied to a better outlook for DRAM and NAND memory, where demand is growing faster than supply. Wolfe also expects pricing strength to last through 2026 and 2027 as AI servers require more memory and new factory capacity remains limited.
High-bandwidth memory is another key part of the story. Caso expects HBM pricing to improve in 2027 as suppliers push for better margins.
For investors, the call adds to the view that Micron is benefiting from one of the strongest memory cycles in years. The next test will be whether earnings and guidance support that optimism.
